newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian T-bills open stronger on tame U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: Canadian T-bills open stronger on tame U.S. data.

text.p: Canadian T-bills opened stronger on Tuesday, amid a widespead rally in fixed-income markets, following the release of weaker-than-expected U.S. economic data, dealers said.

"They were really good numbers for the market, both of them. Growth is there without as much inflationary concern. That may bring the question forward 'Is the Fed going to have to increase rates?'" said a T-bill trader with one bank-owned brokerage.
Canada's three-month when-issued T-bill firmed to yield 3.19 percent from 3.26 percent at Monday's close.

Both Canadian and U.S. fixed-income markets rallied following reports showing U.S. durable goods orders fell more than expected in March, while the U.S. employment cost index for the first quarter rose less than expected.
"Our market has rallied along with it (the U.S. market) and the currency has improved a little bit too," the trader said. "We've seen a flurry of activity after that (news) as you would expect."
The Canadian dollar, which rallied below C$1.40 (US$0.7143) on the news, has been under pressure recently on concern about the possibility of a near-term U.S. rate rise.
In other prices, the six-month when-issued T-bill firmed to yield 3.54 percent from 3.69 percent on Monday. The one-year T-bill firmed to yield 4.17 percent, from 4.35 percent on Monday.
The call loan rate traded at 3.05 percent, near the center of the Bank of Canada's 2.75-3.25 percent target range. ((Jeffrey Hodgson (416) 941-8105, e-mail: jeffrey.hodgson@reuters.com))
